name: Fortress Loans
rootCause: Malicious Proposal & Price Oracle Manipulation. Lost: 1,048.1 ETH + 400,000 DAI (~$3.00M)

descriptions.text: Malicious Proposal & Price Oracle Manipulation. Lost: 1,048.1 ETH + 400,000 DAI (~$3.00M)

Fortress is in ruins after $3M was stolen by an oracle manipulation and malicious governance act. The UI is paused, but the contracts remain live. Will Fortress's ecosystem bail out users for the lost funds?

Insufficient validation in submit() in chain contract. Vulnerable code snippet: https://bscscan.com/address/0xc11b687cd6061a6516e23769e4657b6efa25d78e#code#F1#L142 L142 was commented out. There is no verification to ensure the function call is triggered properly. Anyone can call submit function to manipulate price oracle.

Fortress Protocol, a lending protocol on BNB Chain, was suspected of being attacked. Token FTS fell by 42% in a short time. Currently, 1,048 Ethereum and 400,000 DAI have been transferred to Tornado.cash.

On May 8, 2022, Fortress Loans on BNB Chain was exploited via a combination of malicious governance and price oracle manipulation, resulting in losses totaling 1,048.1 ETH and 400,000 DAI (~$2.98M). The attacker manipulated collateral values by submitting fraudulent price updates and executing a crafted governance proposal. Fortress Loans suffered from two critical flaws: the Chain oracle contract's submit function lacked proper signature and power validation, allowing arbitrary price updates, and the governance design allowed a low-priced token to control malicious proposals, ultimately enabling an attacker to inflate collateral value and drain funds.
